title.justification: The title is clearly stated at the top of the paper, right after the list of authors.

analysis.description: The paper investigates the effects of systems consolidation on behavioral flexibility in mice using a novel Y-maze paradigm. The study concludes that systems consolidation reduces the ability to adapt to changes in the optimal sequence of actions, especially after prolonged delays.

type.justification: The paper presents experiments conducted on mice using a Y-maze paradigm to study the effects of systems consolidation on behavioral flexibility. It includes experimental methodology, data collection, and analysis.
type.quote: Here, we tested how systems consolidation affects: (1) flexibility in response to value changes and (2) flexibility in response to changes in the optimal sequence of actions. Mice were trained to obtain food rewards in a Y-maze by switching nose pokes between three arms.

name.justification: The study focuses on how systems consolidation affects neural mechanisms related to behavioral flexibility, particularly in the hippocampus and medial prefrontal cortex of mice.
name.quote: Understanding the neural mechanisms that promote or hinder this behavioral flexibility is crucial to understanding how animals can survive in a dynamic environment.

name.justification: The primary focus of the paper is on systems consolidation and its impact on neural mechanisms and behavior.
name.quote: Previous research suggests that systems consolidation, a long-term poststorage process that alters memory traces, may reduce behavioral flexibility.

name.justification: The paper is centered around how behavioral flexibility is impacted by systems consolidation.
name.quote: Behavioral flexibility is important in a changing environment.

name.justification: The paper examines the role of the hippocampus in behavioral flexibility as part of systems consolidation.
name.quote: Immediate early gene imaging suggested that the 28 d mice were less reliant on their hippocampus.
